Leo Tolstoy, a Russian author and Christian anarchist, converted to vegetarianism in his later years. His example inspired vegetarian and humanitarian movements. Tolstoy, influenced by William Frey, argued against meat-eating and violence. His vegetarianism was part of a broader philosophy of non-violence and humanitarianism. Mark from Reno, Nevada, inquired about the 'pigeon sheet' used in his golf club's tournament. The term 'pigeon' refers to an easy target or dupe, and pigeon hunters were gamblers who sought out such marks. The pigeon sheet tracks wagers among golfers, with the term coinciding with bird slang in golf. The show suggests not to be the pigeon but to aim for birdies and eagles.

item.title: altogether something
item.description:
【AI 精简版】 AI-condensed version. This text was produced by an LLM from the original article and may omit details. The original link at the end is the only authoritative source.

Why it is here: useful vocabulary, learning value

Curiosity led to exploring adjectives following 'altogether' in British and American English. British English (BrE) uses 'altogether' more frequently with negation and comparatives, often for understatement. American English (AmE) uses it less frequently but similarly for absolute states. Both dialects use 'altogether' to describe absolute states, with BrE allowing comparatives.

Source: Separated by a Common Language | Published: 2026-11-01 14:00 UTC | Difficulty: 40/100
